{{Elections in Minnesota}}

The '''2026 United States Senate election in Minnesota''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Minnesota]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] lieutenant governor [[Peggy Flanagan]] and [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] former journalist [[Michele Tafoya]] are the nominees for their respective parties. Democratic incumbent [[Tina Smith]] is not seeking a second full term.<ref name="buzzing">{{cite news|work=MPR News|access-date=February 13, 2025|last=Bakst|first=Brian|url=https://www.mprnews.org/story/2025/02/13/tina-smith-will-not-run-for-reelection-in-senate-in-2026|date=February 13, 2025|title=Sen. Tina Smith won't seek reelection in 2026, putting Minnesota seat up for grabs|archive-date=April 15, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250415045923/https://www.mprnews.org/story/2025/02/13/tina-smith-will-not-run-for-reelection-in-senate-in-2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

After Smith announced she would not run for re-election, Flanagan and congresswoman [[Angie Craig]] sought the Democratic nomination, which Flanagan won on August 11 with 59% of the vote. Tafoya won the Republican nomination with 52.1% of the vote over Navy SEAL Adam Schwarze and former basketball player [[Royce White]].

This will be the first Senate election in Minnesota without an incumbent since [[2006 United States Senate election in Minnesota|2006]].<ref>{{cite news|work=MPR News|access-date=March 1, 2025|last=Masters|first=Clay|url=https://www.albertleatribune.com/2025/02/an-open-minnesota-senate-seat-is-enticing-to-plenty-but-unclear-how-many-will-take-plunge/|date=February 14, 2025|title=An open Minnesota Senate seat is enticing to plenty but unclear how many will take plunge|archive-date=February 14, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250214155430/https://www.albertleatribune.com/2025/02/an-open-minnesota-senate-seat-is-enticing-to-plenty-but-unclear-how-many-will-take-plunge/|url-status=live}}</ref> Republicans have not won a Senate election in Minnesota since [[2002 United States Senate election in Minnesota|2002]].

== Democratic-Farmer-Labor primary ==
=== Background and campaign ===
Former Minnesota House Speaker [[Melissa Hortman]] was reportedly considering running for the seat before [[2025 shootings of Minnesota legislators|her assassination]] in June 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last1= Nir| first1= David| last2= Singer| first2= Jeff| title= Morning Digest: Ron DeSantis uses 'officially nonexistent' clout to tout wife as successor| url= https://www.the-downballot.com/p/morning-digest-ron-desantis-uses| access-date= April 21, 2025| website= The Downballot| language= en| date= February 25, 2025}}</ref>

The Democratic primary election between Flanagan and Craig was widely seen as a part of the national struggle between the Democratic Party's progressive and moderate factions since the [[2024 U.S. elections]], with endorsements split by ideology.<ref>{{Cite news| last= Kashiwagi| first= Sydney| date= September 5, 2025| title= Craig, Flanagan U.S. Senate race reflects larger fight over [[AIPAC]] while Craig defended accepting them. ''[[Newsweek]]'' called the primary contest an "ideological proxy fight between [[Bernie Sanders]]-style progressivism and [[Bill Clinton]]-esque '[[Third Way]]' centrism".<ref>{{Cite web |last= Rouhandeh| first= Alex| date= December 5, 2025| title= Minnesota Senate Race Emerges as Key Battle in Democratic Party "Civil War"| url= https://www.newsweek.com/minnesota-senate-race-emerges-as-key-battle-in-democratic-party-civil-war-11159629| access-date= December 19, 2025| website= Newsweek| language= en}}</ref>

Craig reportedly had the private backing of the Democratic Senate leadership, including [[Chuck Schumer]], [[Kirsten Gillibrand]], and the [[Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee]] (DSCC), but they did not endorse her.<ref>{{Cite web| last= Lerer| first= Lisa| date= November 24, 2025| title= Chuck Schumer Faces Pushback From a "Fight Club" of Senate Democrats| url= https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/24/us/politics/schumer-democrats-senate-fight-club.html| access-date= December 2, 2025| website= The New York Times| language= en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date= October 17, 2025| title= Schumer Lines up Behind Centrists in Senate Primaries| url= https://readsludge.com/2025/10/17/schumer-lines-up-behind-centrists-in-senate-primaries/| access-date= November 26, 2025| website= Sludge| language= en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| last= Traister| first= Rebecca| date= November 3, 2025| title= It's My Party and I'll Leave When I Want To| url= https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/democratic-party-politicans-gerontocracy-democrats-too-old-rebecca-traister.html| access-date= November 26, 2025| website= Intelligencer| language= en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news| title= Tough primaries complicate Democrats' bid to retake US Senate| url= https://www.semafor.com/article/09/23/2025/tough-primaries-complicate-democrats-bid-to-retake-us-senate| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20250923193914/https://www.semafor.com/article/09/23/2025/tough-primaries-complicate-democrats-bid-to-retake-us-senate| archive-date= September 23, 2025| url-status= live| access-date= December 18, 2025| language= en| last1= Everett| first1= Burgess| last2= Weigel| first2= David| website= [[Semafor (website)|Semafor]]}}</ref><ref name= "sdec11" />

Flanagan and Craig condemned the [[killing of Renée Good]] by an ICE agent amid [[Deportation in the second Trump administration|Trump's mass deportation campaign]]. Flanagan said she supported a "complete and total overhaul" of [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement|ICE]] and criticized Craig for being "politically expedient" and voting for the [[Laken Riley Act]] and a resolution condemning the [[2025 Boulder fire attack]] and expressing gratitude to ICE agents.<ref>{{Cite web |date= January 14, 2026| title= Democrat Calls Her Opponent
